title: SSE sequence-state orchestrator and function-call boundary safety
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Clients using SSE sometimes reconnect and either miss partial frames or receive duplicate function/tool-call events; this causes downstream state divergence and customer-facing inconsistencies. Goal: Define and implement a server-side 'sequence-state orchestrator' that emits compact continuity markers, deterministic chunk envelopes, and an explicit rejoin handshake so clients can resume without duplication or split function-call events. This ticket covers protocol proposal, server/runtime changes, and a compatibility shim for older clients that only understand naive JSONL boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits framed SSE messages with envelope fields: seq, epoch, frag_id, kind (data/tool_start/tool_end/heartbeat/meta), and stable_id
Client can reconnect and provide last-seen seq+stable_id to resume; server will replay at most missing frames and guarantee no duplication of tool_call outputs in 95% synthetic tests
Function/tool-call boundaries are never delivered split across two reconnects; atomicity verified by integration test harness
Compatibility shim: when client indicates legacy-mode, server downgrades to JSONL-compatible framing and sets conservative heartbeat/ack windows documented in API changelog
New metrics emitted: streaming.rejoins.total, streaming.rejoins.duplicate_toolcalls, streaming.rejoin_latency.p50/p95
comments: 2025-02-18 - Ava Chen: Drafted initial protocol proposal. High-level idea: attach a 64-bit seq and 32-bit frag_id to every SSE chunk; include 'kind' so receivers can enforce atomic boundaries for tool calls.

2025-02-19 - Diego Martinez: Investigated existing resume tokens (ENG-314159). We should avoid large opaque tokens in favor of compact tuples (epoch, seq, frag_id) to reduce header size on reconnect requests.

2025-02-20 - Marco Alvarez (review): Concern about duplicate delivery during server failover. Proposal: orchestrator will maintain a transient lease for live connections; on failover, last persisted seq for stream is consulted before resuming.
2025-02-22 - PM feedback (Lina Patel): Customer impact is medium — affected use cases include function-call side effects (webhooks, DB writes). Need roll-forward plan and clear migration docs.
2025-02-24 - Diego Martinez: Implemented server-side envelope encoding prototype; pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298

2025-02-26 - QA (Sana Iqbal): Integration tests added to replay harness that simulate reconnection mid-tool-call; initial run shows 2/50 duplicates due to race at persistence boundary — investigating buffering window increase.

2025-02-28 - Design note: compatibility shim will set header 'X-Redwood-SSE-Version: 1' or 'legacy-1' so clients can negotiate framing mode. Docs PR: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE+Framing+Proposal
notes: - Envelope JSON per chunk (sent as event: data): {"seq": <u64>, "epoch": <u32>, "frag_id": <u32>, "kind": "data|tool_start|tool_end|heartbeat|meta", "stable_id": <string>, "payload": <base64-or-raw>}
- 'stable_id' is a short opaque id derived from request id + model variant; used to detect cross-request merges when clients reconnect to a different backend
- 'frag_id' allows server to split large logical tokens across multiple SSE chunks while preserving order; fragments from same logical token keep same seq range and increasing frag_id
- Client sends: LastSeen: seq, epoch, stable_id in an HTTP POST to /streams/{id}/rejoin or via 'Last-Seen' header when opening SSE connection
- Server validates epoch coherence; if mismatch -> server issues 'resync' meta chunk with snapshot pointer; otherwise server calculates minimal replay window and streams missing envelopes

- Tool-call output must be enclosed between tool_start and tool_end chunks. Server guarantees both marks are delivered as an atomic unit to client on resume by buffering an in-flight tool-call until completion or persisting a tombstone entry indicating completion point.

- For legacy clients (no version header), server will emit simpler JSONL lines with 'boundary' boolean. This reduces feature set (no frag_id) and increases server-side buffering to avoid split tool calls.

- Default heartbeat interval 15s, client may request 5-60s via query param; orchestrator exposes 'soft_ack' window measured in bytes and time; if client lags beyond window, server will issue a 'resync' and fall back to snapshot streaming
- Emit streaming.rejoin.{success,failure,duplicate_toolcall} and expose per-route dashboards in Console

- Mid-tool-call reconnect during server crash: we will prefer durability (persist tool outputs before marking tool_end) which adds 20-50ms P50 for tool-heavy workloads; this trade-off is configurable per-route
